TL;DR Remnant is an innovative rehash of the genres it draws inspiration from.  Worth a look if you are looking for something new in the ARPG scene particularly if you have a friend or two to play with but not without its fair share of bugs that border on feeling like an Early Access title.

Do NOT play this game for:
- A story
- Enjoyable drop in coop with randos
- Looter shooter gear progression
- Quality melee combat

Remnant is an amalgamation of DnD with guns that evokes Dark Souls esque stamina dependent gameplay very loosely tied around a grim survival window dressing.  The lore is paper thin with dialogue trees that seldom offer any consequence resembling choice outside of a few binary decisions in the later game.

Playing coop with randos is a hairpulling experience for numerous reasons.  To start, Remnant leaves the option for players to join your game to the main menu.  If you decide to allow open invites players will join in and be stuck spectating until you make it back to a checkpoint.  This can be as simple as dying but it will generally leave u waiting for longer than you might like as many players seem eager to leave the option on and disregard players entering their game as they AFK at a checkpoint.  Unless they are touching it you won't enter their game.  This system is further convoluted by a need for all players (up to 3) to touch a checkpoint with you to restock or be standing within a few feet of you to fast travel.  With relatively large maps to explore, this can leave you with no ability to leave when you are ready if one player decided to wander off in search of loot since there is no teleport option to allow players to quickly move to the host when they are ready to leave which will often get you kicked by impatient players.  With no option to text in game and horrible voice chat (I have yet to be able to hear players in game even when I can see their mic is active) you often feel very removed from your teammates.  There is no emote system to relay any thoughts you might have either.  As a result, Remnant seems destined to remain a play with friends game if you want any hope of meaningful involvement with it.

Should you have a buddy or two in Discord, Remnant will really have a chance to shine as you will be able to coordinate against hordes of enemies who will attempt to swarm your position, fire projectiles from overhead or take cover and snipe you from far away.  While your partner may outlevel you, gains are not exponential and your ammunition is finite no matter how powerful you become which serves to keep gameplay from becoming a moot point provided you haven't teamed up with someone maxed out as a level 1 noob.

Melee appears to be an option of last resort when you either run out of ammo or just want to finish off an enemy who is nearly dead without waiting for a reload.  It often feels clunky with no defensive option other than your roll/evade mechanic and with the number of enemies rushing your position it is far preferable to shoot everything you can rather than go in hammer blazing.  While the i-frames on your roll are generous you will find a significant amount of recovery animation preventing you from dodging across the map between each swing.  This is further hampered by the fact that you do not recover stamina while swinging your melee weapon. 

Item capacity may need to be looked at down the road as you will be capable of amassing huge stockpiles that offer unlimited ammo, health regen, status cures and buffs with only the expense of time to apply them preventing you from accessing them mid-fight.  The only place this really seems to damage the overall experience in my opinion is the ammo box which fully restores all your ammo with a single use.  It isn't a bad tool but being able to carry as many as you want seems to interfere with the deliberately limited ammo capacity of each gun as you can simply restock between every encounter once you can afford the measly 200 scrap (gold) pricetag.  Once you factor in the plentiful ammo drops from dead enemies it seems to be overkill ensuring that you never have to worry about running out of bullets save for starting from scratch.

Remnant's replay value comes in the form of two higher difficulties which offer better loot drops and the opportunity to hunt for items and boss weapons you won't find in a single playthrough.  While a lot of this boils down to RNG, the excitement of a new run remains high as your environment will not be identical to the first campaign and your opposition will have switched things up as well.  Your loadout can also be swapped with relative ease as maxing out a weapon requires twenty upgrades and even it your weapons aren't quite maxed out they will still be viable if you want to try something new since gains are more similar to Dungeons and Dragons rather than Diablo or Destiny.

The core leveling system involves completing a series of objectives to unlock trait cards which can be leveled up twenty times for a substantial bonus in whatever they might offer.  This can range from extra hit points to better stamina utility, crit chance, melee damage, revive speed and much more.  Every 1500 exp you earn in game will earn you a trait point and you can find them hidden throughout the RNG generated maps including bosses you may not have seen in your own campaign.  This progression system rewards your exploration enough to encourage players to roam even if they are on a second playthrough or just helping guide a friend through their first.

Bugs and errors will likely plague your playthrough at launch although nothing I encountered amounted to much more than restarting at a checkpoint with no major loss of loot.  With death  resulting in the same penalty and being as plentiful as it is I can't say these glitches amounted to anything game breaking but the overall feel of Remnant at launch is consistent with an Early Access title.  I hope the developers continue to iron out its many faults in an effort to produce a unique experience the AAA industry should be envious of.  As of right now, Remnant is more than worthy of your time if you enjoy ARPGs you can play with a buddy.  Wait for a sale if you already have a similar type of game you are working on.
